description_full: Summit Midstream Corporation owns, develops, and operates midstream energy infrastructure assets primarily shale formations in the continental United States. It operates through Rockies, Permian, Piceance, Mid-Con, and Northeast segments. The company owns, develops, and operates natural gas, crude oil, produced water gathering systems, and transmission pipelines. It serves natural gas and crude oil producers. Summit Midstream Corporation was founded in 2009 and is based in Houston, Texas.

Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (9/10).
financial_summary: Summit Midstream Corporation is a small-cap energy business with a $374M market cap on $562M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +31% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -18.2pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The business throws off $45M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.0× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 30% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
